comparison: Both evaluate ROCK enrichment in skeletogenic cells and VEGF-dependence (C4, C34-C37). OpenEval provides more comprehensive coverage including sequence conservation and RNA-seq data (C29-C33), while peer review focuses specifically on immunostaining temporal dynamics. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate ROCK's role through morpholino and pharmacological inhibition (C5, C38-C40, C44-C46, C48). OpenEval includes additional claims about controls and reversibility (C41, C47, C49-C51, C108). Peer review also incorporates cell culture data (C52-C53). Both find the dual approach convincing and SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R3 evaluates cell-autonomous effects in isolated culture (C7, C52-C55), while peer R2 partially overlaps with cell culture claims (C52-C53) but focuses more broadly on ROCK perturbation approaches. Both find evidence SUPPORTED, though addressing somewhat different aspects.

Both evaluate SR-μCT quantitative morphometric analysis (C56-C57, C59-C64). High agreement on differential effects on elongation versus thickness. OpenEval includes C58 not mentioned by peer review. Both find evidence SUPPORTED with strong quantitative backing.

Perfect claim overlap (C65-C69) on calcein staining demonstrating normal calcium uptake under ROCK inhibition. Both accept this as evidence that ROCK acts downstream of calcium acquisition. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C70-C72) on two-pulse calcein labeling showing loss of tip-dominance and reduced elongation rate. Both accept this as evidence for disrupted spatial control of mineral deposition. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate actomyosin component roles (C74-C77, C81). OpenEval includes broader coverage (C8, C73, C78-C80, C109) including cell culture observations. Peer review focuses on differential F-actin versus MyoII effects. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R8 evaluates F-actin organization around spicules (C82-C88, C112), while peer R7 evaluates both this and ROCK-independent F-actin tip enrichment (C82-C83, C85-C86, C88, C90-C95). Partial overlap with agreement on ROCK's role in F-actin organization. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R9 focuses specifically on ROCK-independent F-actin tip enrichment (C90-C96), which peer R7 includes as part of broader F-actin analysis (C90-C95). Both distinguish ROCK's role in tip-dominance from F-actin localization. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate ROCK's role in gene regulation through qPCR and in situ hybridization (C97-C102, C106-C107). OpenEval includes additional claims (C103-C105, C110, C123). Both accept spatial restriction of gene expression and feedback to GRN. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate mechanistic model based on differential phenotypes (C113-C114). OpenEval includes C115-C116 on dose-dependent interpretation. Peer review notes ROCK's dual roles but questions directness. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculation; peer review SUPPORTED for dual roles but implicitly uncertain about mechanisms.

Both address dose-dependent effects and mechanistic interpretation (C115-C116). OpenEval finds model logical but requiring testing (UNCERTAIN). Peer review acknowledges data but notes uncertainty about how direct ROCK's role is (UNCERTAIN). Strong agreement on need for further investigation.

Both evaluate vesicle exocytosis hypothesis (C121-C122). OpenEval notes reasonable but speculative proposal lacking direct evidence (UNCERTAIN). Peer review notes mechanism as potential but requiring investigation, with additional consideration of matrix protein exocytosis (UNCERTAIN). Strong agreement on speculative nature.

Both evaluate mechanotransduction hypothesis (C127, with C123 in peer review). OpenEval notes well-documented gene expression effects but speculative mechanosensing mechanism (UNCERTAIN). Peer review states unclear where ROCK is involved and notes as future work (UNCERTAIN). Strong agreement on uncertainty.

Both evaluate evolutionary synthesis about actomyosin as conserved biomineralization toolkit (C128-C129). OpenEval includes broader context (C9) and finds well-supported by integration with prior work (SUPPORTED). Peer review accepts interpretation without challenge (SUPPORTED). Strong agreement.

OpenEval R15 evaluates background literature claims (C1-C3, C10-C28) as appropriately cited context, finding them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are not primary findings requiring validation.

OpenEval R16 evaluates inhibitor specificity controls (C42-C43, C47, C55), finding convergent evidence SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer review implicitly accepts specificity by not challenging the approach.

OpenEval R17 evaluates descriptive summary of spicule formation (C111) as SUPPORTED context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as this is background information rather than a primary claim requiring validation.
